newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ex-Soviet Georgia wheat output far below target.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Soviet Georgia wheat output far below target.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Georgia is likely to see total wheat output of 177,000 tonnes this year, below the targeted 360,000 tonnes but above last year's level, Interfax news agency said on Friday.
It quoted Georgian Agriculture Minister Bakur Gulua as saying that poor weather had damaged crops and pushed down average yields to 1.5 tonnes per hectare.
The tiny country needs a total of 800,000-850,000 tonnes of grain to meet annual demand, including about 600,000 tonnes of feedgrain and 200,000 tonnes of milling wheat.
Tbilisi recently scrapped all tariffs on grain imports.
The ministry has said that Georgia imported 300,000 tonnes of grain so far this year, of which 80,000 tonnes was in the form of humanitarian aid.
The country has targeted a total 1996 grain crop of 500,000 tonnes, below 1995's 531,000 tonnes. Most of its wheat crop is milling wheat.
Georgia increased the area sown to grain this year to 420,000 hectares from last year's 280,000.
